> Yep, I have a macOS Sequoia 15.6 and can confirm it

As in, it's already broken 2 weeks ago?
But surely if building rustc main on macOS was entirely broken or 2 weeks we'd have heard about it. So there must be something specific to your setup that breaks it?

I tried it first time today, before this I was working only in dev desktop

As for setup I just cloned https://github.com/rust-lang/rust and ran `./x b`

> if building rustc main on macOS was entirely broken or 2 weeks we'd have heard about it.

but yeah, I agree with this, it's odd
I'm trying locally on aarch64 macos against 69b78537fac

I can reproduce with a compiler profile (arm64 macOS 26.2), no download-ci-rustc.

```
  --- stderr
  llvm-config: error: libLLVM-22-rust-1.95.0-nightly.dylib is missing
```

Trying an slightly older commit.

UPD:
- ff0f239bb15 OK
- f02672cb8bf FAIL
- 696a7a1f04c OK
- 1ed488274be FAIL

**Oh**, working theory before I sleep:

- The LLVM update PR itself is not the reason, but it triggers CI LLVM rebuild
- CI LLVM config now has `--linked-shared` from https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/153077

So *maybe* they are somehow related afterall?

```
  llvm-config: error: libLLVM-22-rust-1.95.0-nightly.dylib is missing

  thread 'main' (244946) panicked at compiler/rustc_llvm/build.rs:292:16:
  command did not execute successfully: "/Users/joe.xu/Documents/repos/rust/build/aarch64-apple-darwin/ci-llvm/bin/llvm-config" "--link-shared" "--libs" "--system-libs" "aarch64" "amdgpu" "arm" "asmparser" "avr" "bitreader" "bitwriter" "bpf" "coverage" "csky" "hexagon" "instrumentation" "ipo" "linker" "loongarch" "lto" "m68k" "mips" "msp430" "nvptx" "powerpc" "riscv" "sparc" "systemz" "webassembly" "x86" "xtensa"
```

have not compared if previous invocation has `--linked-shared` or not yet.
Hm, *might* need to wait until the https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/153079 revert lands to have a new CI LLVM / reverted CI LLVM config?

I believe this is a duplicate of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/153077, which is now fixed.

However, due to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/153146, if you use download-ci-llvm, you won't pick up the new LLVM unless you have a shallow clone. A temporary hack I did just to unblock me is to:

```diff
diff --git a/src/bootstrap/src/core/build_steps/llvm.rs b/src/bootstrap/src/core/build_steps/llvm.rs
index 0c607cb6ba6..05503afed88 100644
--- a/src/bootstrap/src/core/build_steps/llvm.rs
+++ b/src/bootstrap/src/core/build_steps/llvm.rs
@@ -194,6 +194,7 @@ pub fn prebuilt_llvm_config(
 
 /// Paths whose changes invalidate LLVM downloads.
 pub const LLVM_INVALIDATION_PATHS: &[&str] = &[
+    "src/ci/github-actions/jobs.yml",
     "src/llvm-project",
     "src/bootstrap/download-ci-llvm-stamp",
     // the LLVM shared object file is named `LLVM-<LLVM-version>-rust-{version}-nightly`
```

Seems to be fixed by https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/153179, cache-busting LLVM did the trick.

Thanks @jieyouxu!
